piles.label: Thranduil's pile
piles.intro: Cards that fit Thranduil's Elves-and-graveyard deck better. Thranduil borrows the activated abilities of Elf cards in your graveyard and loots whenever a legendary Elf enters, so a non-Elf card has to beat an Elf for its slot.

piles.label: Glarb's pile
piles.intro: Cards that fit Glarb's draw-to-mill deck better. Every draw mills the opponent, Bruvac and The Water Crystal multiply it, and Glarb casts mana value 4+ straight off the top.

piles.label: Either deck
piles.intro: Cards that work in both decks: shared removal, ramp and fixing, scry Elves, planeswalkers. Copies are shared in Arena, so one card can sit in both lists.

piles.label: Fits neither
piles.intro: Cards that fit neither deck, each with the reason. Listed so nothing is silently dropped.

Legolas, Counter of Kills.text: **Thranduil:** Legendary Elf body; minor text. **Glarb:** Minor.

Tam, Observant Sequencer // Deep Sight.text: Owned. Draw one on landfall-prepared casts; small.

Elrond, Master of Healing.text: **Thranduil:** Legendary Elf; counters on scry, draws when targeted. **Glarb:** Few creatures to put counters on.

Ezuri, Stalker of Spheres.text: **Re-graded 2026-11-02 (synergy first):** Up from ◇: proliferate sources went 1→3 (High Perfect Morcant, Vraska, Yawgmoth's discard: proliferate). It proliferates twice on ETB across 7 planeswalkers, and as a legendary Elf it is also a Thranduil loot. **Earlier:** "Whenever you proliferate, draw a card" — the deck has one proliferate source (Vraska, Betrayal's Sting).

Jyoti, Moag Ancient.text: Needs commander recasts and land creatures.

Kiora, the Crashing Wave.text: **Thranduil:** −1 draw + extra land; +1 fogs one threat. **Glarb:** Same.

Nael, Avizoa Aeronaut.text: **Re-graded 2026-11-02 (synergy first):** Up from ✗: the draw is still dead (Sultai lands reach 3 types). But as a legendary Elf it is a Thranduil loot on a 4-mana flier with combat card selection, so it is below the bar, not off-plan. **Earlier:** Domain: Sultai lands give at most 3 basic types, so "if there are five … draw a card" never happens.

Rashmi, Eternities Crafter.text: **Thranduil:** Legendary Elf; a free spell off the top each turn. Bench in both. **Glarb:** Same, and the top card is visible under Glarb, so you know when it hits.

Imoti, Celebrant of Bounty.text: Cascade on mana value 6+ — the deck has few 6+ spells.

Kruphix, God of Horizons.text: Hand-size enabler only; rarely a creature in three colours.

Tamiyo, Compleated Sage.text: "−X: Exile target nonland permanent card with mana value X from your graveyard" — Same; the +1 tap is tempo, not removal.

Tawnos, the Toymaker.text: Copies Beasts/Birds; neither deck has them.

Oko, the Trickster.text: Six mana for counters; weak here.

Bonny Pall, Clearcutter.text: **Re-graded 2026-11-02 (synergy first):** Unchanged at ★★. Repeatable draw plus lands back from the yard (milled by Wrenn and Seven, Wrenn and Realmbreaker, Sidisi), and landfall feeds Sindarin Liege tokens. Only the 6-mana UU cost holds it back. **Earlier:** 6 mana; "Whenever you attack, draw a card, then … put a land card from your hand or graveyard onto the battlefield" — real value, wrong curve slot beside Selvala/Kamahl's Vow.

Tishana, Voice of Thunder.text: Draws one per creature you control — usually 2–4 here; 7 mana.

Kotis, Sibsig Champion.text: "cast a creature spell from your graveyard by exiling three other cards from your graveyard" — Three cards a turn, in a yard that is mostly Elves; Muldrotha recasts without exiling anything.

Leovold, Emissary of Trest.text: In Thranduil's list. **Why not Glarb's:** "Each opponent can't draw more than one card each turn" switches off Dictate of Kruphix and Seizan's extra draws for them — it fights this deck's mill.

Nashi, Moon's Legacy.text: **Re-graded 2026-11-02 (synergy first):** Holds at ★★★, and "legends are mostly Elves" is now false: 23 non-Elf legendary nonland cards against 15 Elves (Vile Offering, Kamahl's Vow, the walkers, Yarok, Sidisi). The G-42 cost is avoidable, and the exile triggers Teval, Oasis and Roots. **Earlier:** "exile up to one target legendary or Rat card from your graveyard and copy it" — Can target a non-Elf legend, but the deck's legends ARE mostly Elves; menace 3-drop otherwise.

Nashi, Illusion Gadgeteer.text: **Re-graded 2026-11-02 (synergy first):** Holds at ★★ (drops the ◇ hedge). It is recursion that leaves the original in Thranduil's yard, with no G-42 cost. Yarok (new) doubles the ETB into two cards. **Earlier:** Conjures a copy of a yard card into hand (keeps the original — no G-42 cost); a 4-mana non-Elf. ◇

Kotis, the Fangkeeper.text: Exiles X on combat damage and casts them free — an aggressive card in a deck that wins by milling.

Sidisi, Brood Tyrant.text: **Re-graded 2026-11-02 (synergy first):** Holds at ★★★, and "the Zombies feed nothing Elf-gated" is void. The Zombies now feed Yawgmoth's sac-draw, Insidious Roots mana, Eladamri and Circle of Dreams, and Yarok doubles the ETB mill. **Earlier:** Not an Elf, and its mill is random where Thranduil's loot chooses — Mills three on entry and attack; with 45 creatures most mills make a 2/2 Zombie. Strong, just not Elf-synergistic (the Zombies feed nothing Elf-gated).

Gonti, Canny Acquisitor.text: Steals a card on combat damage; the deck is a control deck that rarely connects.

Brokkos, Apex of Forever.text: **Re-graded 2026-11-02 (synergy first):** Unchanged at ★, with a better reason than "adds a body". Each recast from the yard triggers Teval, Oasis of Renewal and Insidious Roots, plus Kotis (new) for a graveyard cast, and mutate keeps an Elf's tap ability. The payoffs must already be on board. **Earlier:** Recursive mutate threat; Elves are non-Human so it can mutate, but it adds a body, not an engine.

Maralen, Fae Ascendant.text: In Thranduil's list. **Why not Glarb's:** Exiles two of their library per Elf or Faerie entering — this deck has almost none.

Yarok, the Desecrated.text: **Thranduil:** If a permanent entering causes a trigger "that ability triggers an additional time" — Thranduil's legendary-Elf loot becomes draw 4, discard 2, and every Elf ETB doubles. **Strong add.** **Glarb:** Doubles Sphinx Mindbreaker (mill 20) and Sheoldred's edict, but few ETBs here.

Sin, Spira's Punishment.text: **Re-graded 2026-11-02 (synergy first):** Holds at ★★, but the G-42 objection is replaced by the owner's exception: an exiled Elf's ability moves to the token. A land hit is upside (a free tapped land, then repeat). The real costs are 7 mana and randomly stealing a Kotis/Muldrotha recast target. **Earlier:** "exile a permanent card from your graveyard at random" — Random — will hit Elves; 7 mana.

Mimeoplasm, Revered One.text: "exile up to X creature cards from your graveyard" — Eats exactly the Elf creature cards Thranduil borrows from.

Glamdring, Foe-hammer // Gleam of Death.text: An Equipment for an instants deck.

Fblthp, Impossibly Lost.text: **Thranduil:** Draw two on combat damage. **Glarb:** Rarely attacks.

Jace Reawakened.text: **Thranduil:** Loot every turn — feeds the yard. **Glarb:** Loot draws mill two.

Marit Lage's Slumber.text: Needs snow permanents; neither deck has any.

Mystic Reflection.text: Copies a nonlegendary creature; same problem as Mindlink Mech.

Malcolm, Alluring Scoundrel.text: **Re-graded 2026-11-02 (synergy first):** Down from ★. The non-Elf objection is void, but on a 2-power flier the loot is combat-gated, so it is situational. **Earlier:** Combat-gated loot on a non-Elf flier.

Naban, Dean of Iteration.text: Doubles Wizard ETBs; neither deck is Wizards.

Proft's Eidetic Memory.text: Draws one, no hand size, counters on combat — the counters do nothing here.

Rona, Herald of Invasion // Rona, Tolari.text: **Re-graded 2026-11-02 (synergy first):** Unchanged at ★★, now judged on synergy, not "closest to an Elf". A 2-mana loot that untaps off 38 legendary spells fills Thranduil's yard several times a turn, plus Elrond draws and Ioreth untaps. Card-neutral, so not ★★★. **Earlier:** Loot that untaps on legendary spells — the closest of the looters, since most of the deck is legendary.

The Key to the Vault.text: Equipment that casts from YOUR library on combat damage — combat-gated.

Vnwxt, Verbose Host.text: Speed needs opponent life loss; slow in both.

Arni, Humble Scribe.text: **Re-graded 2026-11-02 (synergy first):** Grade holds, but "lost to an Elf" is void. It is a 3-mana loot that untaps off 45 creatures, so it bins Elves for Thranduil, and its tap ability triggers Elrond. A real add candidate. **Earlier:** `{T}: Draw a card, then discard a card` duplicates Thranduil's own loot; lost to an Elf.

Chandra, Chill of Compliance.text: Owned. +1 surveil feeds Matoya and Proft; the other +1 adds mana for noncreature spells; −X stuns a threat. Screened KEY against the list.

Callaphe, Beloved of the Sea.text: A mild ward tax; no engine.

Elrond, Lord of Rivendell.text: **Thranduil:** Legendary Elf; scry 1 per creature entering — modest. **Glarb:** Each scry triggers Matoya — a draw per creature entering. Close.

Elrond, Moon-Reader.text: In Thranduil's list. **Why not Glarb's:** "Whenever you activate an ability of a creature, draw a card" (once a turn) — Glarb's own surveil tap triggers it, so every turn is a draw that mills two. **Good add here too.**

Fblthp, Lost on the Range.text: Plots from the top — a slower version of what Glarb already does.

Geralf, the Fleshwright.text: Needs several cheap spells a turn.

Graviton, Fundamental Force.text: Draw-trigger tapper — minor in Glarb's deck.

Impossible Man.text: Clone utility without a target worth copying every turn.

Ioreth of the Healing House.text: **Thranduil:** `{T}: Untap two other target legendary creatures` — untap Thranduil for a second borrowed {T} ability each turn (Dionus's job, again). **Strong add.** **Glarb:** Untaps Glarb for a second surveil 2, which Matoya turns into a second draw. Real, smaller.

Katara, Bending Prodigy.text: A weak body for either deck.

Kira, Great Glass-Spinner.text: Counters the first targeting of each creature — including your own pump or untap (Ioreth, Dionus).

Lyra, Tolarian Archangel.text: Owned. A 3/3 Angel at end step when you drew three — common here, but it is a body, not a draw or a mill.

Mindlink Mech.text: Copies a nonlegendary creature; both decks are mostly legends.

Unctus, Grand Metatect.text: Rummage on blue artifact creatures; few here.

Alora, Rogue Companion.text: Evasion that returns the creature to hand — tempo only.

Arwen's Gift.text: Scry 2, draw 2 (cheaper with two legends); one-shot.

Charix, the Raging Isle.text: Counts Islands; three-colour decks run only a few.

Gale, Conduit of the Arcane.text: Pays off instants/sorceries; Thranduil runs 8, and Glarb's 21 already have better payoffs.

God-Eternal Kefnet.text: Copies instants/sorceries drawn — Glarb sees the top, but Kefnet wants them first-drawn each turn; minor.

Gandalf, Friend of the Shire.text: Ring-tempt payoff; neither deck tempts the Ring.

Irenicus's Vile Duplication.text: Clones a legend — strong only with one ETB engine to copy.

Jace, the Perfected Mind.text: In Glarb's list. **Why not Thranduil's:** −X mills yourself 3X — self-mill on demand; `{2}{U}{U/P}`.

Jace, Wielder of Mysteries.text: +1 mills two and draws one (four milled under Corrosion); its alt-win needs YOUR library empty, which this deck never aims for. `{1}{U}{U}{U}` is hard in three colours.

Leader, Super-Genius.text: **Re-graded 2026-11-02 (synergy first):** Up from ★★: "duplicates Thranduil's loot on a non-Elf" is void. Draw two, discard one every turn, from the turn it lands, is net card advantage plus a discard into the yard, the engine synergy-first ranks first. **Earlier:** Connive each combat; duplicates Thranduil's loot on a non-Elf body.

Multiversal Recruitment.text: **Thranduil:** Copy Priest of Titania or Voice of the Woods, flashback later. Fine. **Glarb:** "Create a token that's a copy of target creature you control, except it isn't legendary" — a second Bruvac quadruples every mill. **Spicy add.**

Orvar, the All-Form.text: Needs instants that target your own permanents.

Taeko, the Patient Avalanche.text: A blink/bounce payoff; no blink in either deck.

The Clone Saga.text: **Thranduil:** Surveil 3 fills the yard; II copies a creature spell. **Glarb:** Surveil 3 triggers Matoya and Proft.

Tui and La, Moon and Ocean.text: An attacker draw engine; neither deck attacks enough.

Vesuvan Duplimancy.text: Needs spells that target your creatures.

Yue, the Moon Spirit.text: A noncreature-spells payoff; both decks are creature-heavy or draw-heavy.

Jace, Memory Adept.text: In Glarb's list. **Why not Thranduil's:** Its 0 "Target player mills ten cards" can target YOU — ten cards of Elves for Thranduil. **Good add here too.**

Jace, Unraveler of Secrets.text: 5 mana; +1 scry 1 then draw (Matoya draws again). Close; −2 bounce is tempo.

Krang, the All-Powerful.text: "If a player drawing a card causes a triggered ability of a permanent you control to trigger, that ability triggers an additional time" doubles Psychic Corrosion, both Tutelages, Sheoldred and The Theorist — the deck's whole engine. **Strongest add on this list.** Left out on slot count.

Pharaoh Rama-Tut.text: **Re-graded 2026-11-02 (synergy first):** Down from ★. The non-Elf objection is void, but only 19 of 64 nonland cards trigger it, so it is a 5-mana card-neutral loot that fires about once a turn at best. **Earlier:** Connives on noncreature spells — 19 here; a non-Elf looter.

Syr Elenora, the Discerning.text: A hand-size body; Glarb's deck has better.

Thryx, the Sudden Storm.text: Spells with mana value 5+ cost {1} less and can't be countered — a flash flier; the deck's MV 5+ spells mostly come off the top already.

Kitsune, Dragon's Daughter.text: **Thranduil:** 6 mana: swap a weak creature of yours for their best. **Glarb:** Same; mana value 6, so Glarb can cast it off the top.

Pol Jamaar, Illusionist.text: Missed by the pile pass. "Choose a creature type. Draw a card for each creature you control of that type" — name Elf, usually 4–6 cards. A 6-mana flier, so a bench-level add.

Jin-Gitaxias, Progress Tyrant.text: Copies your first artifact/instant/sorcery each turn — a second Traumatize empties a library — and counters the opponent's first one. Mana value 7, so Glarb casts it off the top.

The Magic Mirror.text: `{6}{U}{U}{U}` and wants instants/sorceries in the yard.

Wan Shi Tong, Librarian.text: Owned. Flash X body that draws half X, and more when they search; decent filler.

Gadwick, the Wizened.text: Draw X for `{X}{U}{U}{U}` — triple blue in a three-colour deck.

Aphelia, Viper Whisperer.text: An attack-for-value 2-drop; neither deck is an attacking deck.

Reezug, the Bonecobbler.text: Casts a creature card from the yard as an artifact; recasting an Elf takes its ability off Thranduil.

Splinter, the Mentor.text: Its partner text does nothing in Brawl.

Azula, Ruthless Firebender.text: A discard-on-attack outlet; Thranduil already loots, Glarb rarely attacks.

Gix, Yawgmoth Praetor.text: Combat draws; its `{4}{B}{B}{B}` exile needs a hand to discard.

Isareth the Awakener.text: **Re-graded 2026-11-02 (synergy first):** Unchanged at ★★. The G-42 cost now applies only by choice: the yard holds non-Elf ETB targets (Cloud of Darkness, Silumgar, Sheoldred, Overlord) and Yarok doubles their triggers. **Earlier:** Reanimates on attack for {X}, but the returned creature is exiled if it leaves — and the reanimated Elf no longer lends Thranduil its ability.

Kaervek, the Punisher.text: "exile up to one target black card from your graveyard and copy it" — Needs crimes; few black cards to copy outside the Elf core.

Yahenni, Undying Partisan.text: A sac outlet with nothing to sacrifice for value.

Davriel, Soul Broker.text: **Thranduil:** −3 perpetual −3/−3; +1 taxes attackers. Real removal the classifier misses. **Glarb:** Same.

Doctor Doom, Unrivaled.text: **Re-graded 2026-11-02 (synergy first):** Holds at ★★; the "non-Elf" note is void. A repeatable tap-draw is first-priority card advantage, and it triggers Elrond. Ioreth (new) untaps it for a second draw. **Earlier:** In Glarb's list. **Why not Thranduil's:** `{T}: draw a card` on a 4-mana lifelink body — fine; non-Elf.

Erebos, God of the Dead.text: **Thranduil:** `{1}{B}, Pay 2 life: Draw a card`. **Glarb:** Same, and each draw mills two.

Gisa, Glorious Resurrector.text: **Re-graded 2026-11-02 (synergy first):** Down from ★. It touches nothing in our yard and only fires after removal; the decayed bodies feed Yawgmoth, but that is a board-state payoff. **Earlier:** Steals THEIR dead creatures for a turn; off-plan here (a better fit for a removal-heavy deck).

Kels, Fight Fixer.text: Sacrifice payoff; the deck has no sacrifice engine (Yawgmoth would be the outlet, see A).

Liliana of the Dark Realms.text: Counts Swamps; three-colour decks run few.

Lo and Li, Royal Advisors.text: `{2}{U/B}: Target player mills four cards`, repeatable at instant speed; an Advisor (with Bruvac and The Master of Lake-town) that grows when they mill.

Madame Hydra, Reanimated.text: **Re-graded 2026-11-02 (synergy first):** Unchanged at ★★, and "bodies want to be Elves" is void. Repeatable self-mill (doubled on ETB by Yarok, Sidisi Zombies off creature mills) on a body that grows with a 45-creature deck's yard. **Earlier:** Self-mill 2 per attack and grows with creature cards; a non-Elf 4-drop beater in a deck whose bodies want to be Elves.

Massacre Girl, Known Killer.text: Wither plus draw — good against go-wide, off-plan for both.

Moonstone, Harsh Mistress.text: **Re-graded 2026-11-02 (synergy first):** Holds at ★★ (drops the ◇ hedge). The exile is a "may": keep Elf discards for Thranduil and replay non-Elf ones. That makes Thranduil's loot, Fauna Shaman and Yawgmoth's discard (new) card-positive. **Earlier:** Not an Elf — "Whenever you discard a card, you may exile that card … you may play that card" — every Thranduil loot becomes card-neutral. But it EXILES the discard, which removes an Elf's ability from Thranduil (G-42), so it is best with non-Elf discards. ◇

One Ring to Rule Them All.text: **Thranduil:** Chapter II "Destroy all nonlegendary creatures" kills most of the Elves. **Glarb:** II is nearly one-sided here (6 nonlegendary creatures), I mills each player by your Ring-bearer's power, and III drains for each creature card in THEIR graveyard — which the mill fills. **Strong add.**

Rev, Tithe Extractor.text: Treasure + steal on combat damage — same problem.

Yawgmoth, Thran Physician.text: **Re-graded 2026-11-02 (synergy first):** Up from ★★ (now in the list): "not an Elf" is void. A free repeatable sac-draw (fodder from Imperious Perfect, Sidisi, Liege, Morcant's Eyes, Izoni) puts nontoken Elves into Thranduil's yard, and the discard-proliferate bins cards and ticks 7 walkers. **Earlier:** Not an Elf; the deck runs no dedicated sacrifice outlet — `Pay 1 life, Sacrifice another creature: -1/-1 counter … and draw a card` is repeatable removal plus card draw off the Elf tokens (Imperious Perfect, Elvish Warmaster, Voice of the Woods, Lathril).

Whisper, Blood Liturgist.text: Sacrifice two to reanimate — costly without tokens.

Aclazotz, Deepest Betrayal // Temple of.text: **Re-graded 2026-11-02 (synergy first):** Down from ★★: the "no Elf" half is void, but synergy-first puts off-engine power behind engine cards. It feeds no graveyard, makes no mana and draws only off an empty hand, in a crowded 5-drop slot. **Earlier:** A 5-mana flier with hand attack; strong card, no Elf or graveyard tie.

Ashiok, Wicked Manipulator.text: "If you would pay life … exile that many cards from the top of your library instead" — Phyrexian Arena, Doctor Doom and Infernal Grasp would exile YOUR library in a deck that already draws hard. Its −7 is a real finisher; the static is the problem.

Black Widow, Daring Operative.text: **Re-graded 2026-11-02 (synergy first):** Down from ★★: the ETB mill 3 is real fuel and Yarok doubles it. But the payoff is combat-gated on a 5-drop, and Dawnhand Eulogist already does this for 4. **Earlier:** Mill 3 then drains = creature cards in yard on combat damage — combat-gated, 5 mana.

Drana, the Last Bloodchief.text: **Re-graded 2026-11-02 (synergy first):** Unchanged at ★. Recursion every attack now also triggers the leave-the-yard payoffs and Kotis. The opponent still picks (the worst of ~18 nonlegendary creatures, usually an Elf whose ability Thranduil was using). **Earlier:** "defending player chooses a nonlegendary creature card" — the OPPONENT picks, so they give you a mana Elf.

Garruk, Veiled Butcher.text: In Thranduil's list. **Why not Glarb's:** Interaction (+2 shrink, −2 edict) and −3 card advantage; the deck's interaction is already 16.

Ghoulcaller Gisa.text: **Re-graded 2026-11-02 (synergy first):** Unchanged at ★. Sacrificing a nontoken Elf moves its ability into Thranduil's yard, and the tap ability triggers Elrond. Yawgmoth (new) now does the sac-outlet job better, with a card drawn. **Earlier:** Sac outlet that makes Zombies = power; Elves are small, so X is 1–2.

Gisa, the Hellraiser.text: **Thranduil:** Zombies on crimes (any removal you aim at them) — off-tribe. **Glarb:** Same.

Junji, the Midnight Sky.text: **Re-graded 2026-11-02 (synergy first):** Unchanged at ★★; "wants Elves in the yard, not Dragons" is void. Its death trigger reanimates, sac outlets (Yawgmoth new, Izoni, Vraska +2) make it fire on demand, and Kotis or Muldrotha can recast it. **Earlier:** A 5-mana flier whose value is its death trigger; the deck wants Elves in the yard, not Dragons.

Lo and Li, Twin Tutors.text: Tutors a Noble: Thranduil's deck has Elrond, Moon-Reader and Maralen, Glarb's has Princess Yue. Thin targets.

Maha, Its Feathers Night.text: **Thranduil:** Their creatures have base toughness 1 — pairs with Gloom Ripper. Flier. **Glarb:** A big flier.

Sauron, the Necromancer.text: "Whenever Sauron attacks, exile target creature card from your graveyard" — Same tax each attack; the token is temporary.

Seizan, Perverter of Truth.text: "At the beginning of each player's upkeep, that player loses 2 life and draws two cards": the opponent loses two library cards a turn, and your two draws mill four through Psychic Corrosion. Symmetric, which this deck wants (it already runs Dictate of Kruphix).

Seymour Flux.text: Pay 1 life: draw one each upkeep — a Phyrexian Arena on a body, and Arena is in.

Shredder, Shadow Master.text: A combat finisher with no synergy.

Syr Konrad, the Grim.text: Pings on every creature death, mill and leave-graveyard; strong in a self-mill deck, but 5 mana for 1-point pings. Bench.

Tergrid, God of Fright // Tergrid's Lant.text: Needs the opponent to sacrifice or discard; neither deck forces it often.

Witch-king of Angmar.text: A defensive edict against attackers; Ring tempt unused.

Doctor Doom.text: **Thranduil:** Two 3/3 Doombots and a draw each end step for 6. **Glarb:** The end-step draw mills two.

Bolas's Citadel.text: Glarb already casts MV 4+ off the top; Citadel adds the cheap ones for life. `{3}{B}{B}{B}` with 20 black sources, and the life matters against aggro.

Ink-Eyes, Servant of Oni.text: Reanimates THEIR creature on combat damage — both decks rarely connect.

Lich's Mastery.text: Losing life exiles your own permanents; too risky in both.

The Cloning of Shredder.text: "Exile target creature card from your graveyard" — Six mana for copies of a card Thranduil was already using.

Vraska, Betrayal's Sting.text: In Thranduil's list. **Why not Glarb's:** 0: draw (mills two) and proliferate; −2 neutralises a creature. A fine add; 6 mana.

K'rrik, Son of Yawgmoth.text: Life-for-mana with no black-pip payoff worth it.

Morlun, Devourer of Spiders.text: An X-cost beater; its drain hits only opponents.

Celeborn the Wise.text: **Re-graded 2026-11-02 (synergy first):** Down from ◇: synergy-first demotes Elf-only text. Its one real contribution is the Thranduil loot as a legendary Elf entering; it has no activated ability for the yard. **Earlier:** "Whenever you attack with one or more Elves, scry 1" and a pump — combat-only, minor.

Leyline Immersion.text: **Thranduil:** On Thranduil: ward 2 and `{T}`: five mana for spells — but it spends the {T} he uses for borrowed abilities. **Glarb:** Same on Glarb: it spends his surveil tap.

Mythweaver Poq.text: Land ramp off a narrow trigger.

Radagast of Rhosgobel.text: First creature each turn costs {2} less with flash; 20 creatures, few of them cheap.

Tyvar Kell.text: Missed by the pile pass (graded for the old graveyard plan). "Elves you control have `{T}: Add {B}`" fixes black on all 11 mana Elves, 0 makes an Elf every turn, +1 untaps one, and the −6 emblem draws two per Elf spell. **Strong add.**

Ashaya, Soul of the Wild.text: Makes your creatures lands — no landfall payoff to cash it in.

Bosco, Just a Bear.text: Food with no Food payoff in either deck.

Greensleeves, Maro-Sorcerer.text: Landfall threat; neither deck plays extra lands often.

Skemfar Avenger.text: "Whenever another nontoken Elf or Berserker you control dies, you draw a card" — **Thranduil:** Only draws on a nontoken Elf dying, and the deck has 2 sac outlets (owner cut it). **Glarb:** No Elves, so it is off-plan.

Morcant's Loyalist.text: "When this creature dies, return another target Elf card from your graveyard to your hand." — **Thranduil:** Lord plus a death trigger that pulls an Elf tool OUT of Thranduil's yard; cut 2026-11-02 as Elf-only. **Glarb:** Elf lord with no draw, mill or interaction text.

Gloom Ripper.text: "…gets -0/-X … where X is the number of Elves you control plus the number of Elf cards in your graveyard." — **Thranduil:** In list: X runs large with 33 Elves plus the yard, so it's real removal on a body; 5 mana keeps it from ★★. **Glarb:** X is about 1 here, so it's dead.

Leaf-Crowned Visionary.text: "Whenever you cast an Elf spell, you may pay {G}. If you do, draw a card." — **Thranduil:** Repeatable card draw off 33 Elf spells is real CA; the lord half is tiebreaker value only. **Glarb:** No Elf spells to trigger it; off-plan.

Shaman of the Pack.text: "target opponent loses life equal to the number of Elves you control" — **Thranduil:** A one-shot drain sized by Elf count with no graveyard, mana or card synergy (owner cut it). **Glarb:** Drains about 1 with no Elves.

Morcant's Eyes.text: "At the beginning of your upkeep, surveil 1. … Create X 2/2 black and green Elf creature tokens, where X is the number of Elf cards in your graveyard." — **Thranduil:** Bins an Elf every upkeep, then cashes the full Elf yard into tokens. **Glarb:** The upkeep surveil triggers Matoya and Proft for a draw; the token half is dead here.

Bounty of Skemfar.text: "…up to one land card … onto the battlefield tapped and up to one Elf card … into your hand." — **Thranduil:** A land and an Elf only; the owner cut it as Elf-only value. **Glarb:** The Elf half is dead and the rest goes to the bottom.

Harald Unites the Elves.text: "I — Mill three cards. You may put an Elf or Tyvar card from your graveyard onto the battlefield." — **Thranduil:** Self-mill plus a free Elf reanimation (a legendary one loots); trades that Elf's borrowed ability for the body. **Glarb:** Elf saga with nothing to reanimate or pump; off-plan.

Insidious Roots.text: "Whenever one or more creature cards leave your graveyard, create a 0/1 green Plant" — **Thranduil:** Muldrotha, Kotis, reanimation, Deathrite and Overlord all trigger it, and Elf/Zombie tokens tap for any colour. **Glarb:** Creature cards rarely leave its own yard and it makes few tokens.

Overlord of the Balemurk.text: "Whenever this permanent enters or attacks, mill four cards, then you may return a non-Avatar creature card or a planeswalker card from your graveyard to your hand." — **Thranduil:** Two-mana impending self-mill plus recursion, repeated on attacks: the deck's exact engine. **Glarb:** Own-yard mill and recursion isn't the plan; at most it returns one threat.

Trystan's Command.text: "Return one or two target permanent cards from your graveyard to your hand. • Destroy target creature or enchantment." — **Thranduil:** In list: recursion plus removal in one card; core keep. **Glarb:** Castable, but a 6-mana sorcery removal spell in a deck already deep in cheaper answers; the recursion and Elf modes do little.

Heartless Act.text: "Destroy target creature with no counters on it." — **Thranduil:** Two-mana instant removal for a deck that needs interaction; a core keep. **Glarb:** Premium cheap instant removal; would make most versions of the control list.

Go for the Throat.text: "Destroy target nonartifact creature." — **Thranduil:** Cheap instant removal in a deck that needs interaction. **Glarb:** Cheap instant removal for a control deck.

Infernal Grasp.text: "Destroy target creature. You lose 2 life." — **Thranduil:** Two-mana instant unconditional removal in a list whose interaction comes from outside the pile. **Glarb:** Same: cheap instant removal is a core keep in a control deck.

Command Tower.text: "{T}: Add one mana of any color in your commander's color identity." — **Thranduil:** Untapped three-colour land; core. **Glarb:** Untapped three-colour land; core.

Eclipsed Realms.text: "{T}: Add one mana of any color. Spend this mana only to cast a spell of the chosen type or activate an ability of a source of the chosen type." — **Thranduil:** Naming Elf, its colour pays for 33 Elves and Thranduil's borrowed Elf abilities; colourless otherwise. **Glarb:** No creature of a listed type to name, so it taps for {C} in a three-colour pip deck.

Overgrown Tomb.text: "({T}: Add {B} or {G}.) … you may pay 2 life" — **Thranduil:** An untapped typed B/G dual that enables Woodland Cemetery and Wastewood Verge. **Glarb:** An untapped typed dual that enables the checklands.

Breeding Pool.text: "({T}: Add {G} or {U}.) As this land enters, you may pay 2 life." — **Thranduil:** Untapped typed dual; enables Hinterland Harbor and Wastewood Verge. **Glarb:** Untapped G/U dual covering the green splash and blue core.

Watery Grave.text: "({T}: Add {U} or {B}.) …you may pay 2 life." — **Thranduil:** In list: an untapped dual, though the off-pair for a G/B-heavy list. **Glarb:** In list: untapped U/B, this deck's main pair.

Woodland Cemetery.text: "This land enters tapped unless you control a Swamp or a Forest. {T}: Add {B} or {G}." — **Thranduil:** Usually-untapped B/G dual for the {B}{B} cards; a strong manabase keep. **Glarb:** Usually-untapped B/G dual; a strong manabase keep.

Hinterland Harbor.text: "enters tapped unless you control a Forest or an Island" — **Thranduil:** A G/U checkland that is usually untapped with the deck's typed lands. **Glarb:** Usually untapped, but G/U is the less important pair here.

Drowned Catacomb.text: "This land enters tapped unless you control an Island or a Swamp. {T}: Add {U} or {B}." — **Thranduil:** U/B is the list's lightest pair; a fine but replaceable dual. **Glarb:** U/B is this deck's core pair and 12 basic Islands/Swamps keep it untapped.

Llanowar Wastes.text: "{T}: Add {B} or {G}. This land deals 1 damage to you." — **Thranduil:** In list: untapped B/G, the deck's main pair. **Glarb:** In list: untapped, but B/G is the minor pair here.

Yavimaya Coast.text: "{T}: Add {G} or {U}. This land deals 1 damage to you." — **Thranduil:** Always-untapped G/U source; ping is minor at 25 life. **Glarb:** Always-untapped G/U source; strong manabase keep.

Underground River.text: "{T}: Add {U} or {B}. This land deals 1 damage to you." — **Thranduil:** An untapped U/B painland, U being the deck's lightest colour. **Glarb:** U/B is the deck's core pair and this land is always untapped.

Clearwater Pathway // Murkwater Pathway.text: "{T}: Add {U}. // {T}: Add {B}." — **Thranduil:** Untapped, chosen for B sources in the draft; one colour once played. **Glarb:** Untapped U or B, but only one of them per game.

Zagoth Triome.text: "({T}: Add {B}, {G}, or {U}.) This land enters tapped. Cycling {3}" — **Thranduil:** In list: all three colours and three basic types (turns on the checklands and the Verge). **Glarb:** In list: all three colours with cycling; the tapped entry is fine in control.

Underground Mortuary.text: "This land enters tapped. When this land enters, surveil 1." — **Thranduil:** Surveil bins an Elf for Thranduil; owner kept the surveil lands for exactly that. **Glarb:** Surveil triggers Matoya and Proft (a draw, which mills); worth the tapped entry.

Hedge Maze.text: "This land enters tapped. When this land enters, surveil 1." — **Thranduil:** A tapped surveil land that bins an Elf for Thranduil (the notes keep it). **Glarb:** Its surveil triggers Matoya and Proft, but it enters tapped.

Undercity Sewers.text: "This land enters tapped. When this land enters, surveil 1." — **Thranduil:** Tapped, but the surveil bins an Elf for Thranduil (the notes keep it for that). **Glarb:** Tapped, but the surveil triggers Matoya/Proft.

Darkslick Shores.text: "This land enters tapped unless you control two or fewer other lands." — **Thranduil:** In list: U/B is the minor pair, and it's usually tapped late in 100 cards. **Glarb:** In list: U/B, the main pair.

Blooming Marsh.text: "This land enters tapped unless you control two or fewer other lands." — **Thranduil:** B/G dual that is untapped only early; real but a tier below the check/shock lands. **Glarb:** Untapped only early in a long control game; a real but replaceable dual.

Botanical Sanctum.text: "enters tapped unless you control two or fewer other lands" — **Thranduil:** An untapped G/U land early; G is the main colour. **Glarb:** A late-tapped G/U fastland in a deck whose core pair is U/B.

Wastewood Verge.text: "{T}: Add {G}. {T}: Add {B}. Activate only if you control a Swamp or a Forest." — **Thranduil:** Untapped G with gated B; added in the draft for B sources. **Glarb:** No blue, and green is this list's splash (2 Forests).

Darkbore Pathway // Slitherbore Pathway.text: "{T}: Add {B}. // {T}: Add {G}." — **Thranduil:** In list: an untapped B or G source for the {B}{B} cards. **Glarb:** In list: untapped but one colour only, from the minor pair.

Psychic Corrosion.text: "Whenever you draw a card, each opponent mills two cards." — **Thranduil:** Opponent mill is off-plan for a self-graveyard deck. **Glarb:** The deck's core draw-to-mill engine (protected).

Teferi's Tutelage.text: "Whenever you draw a card, target opponent mills two cards." — **Thranduil:** Opponent-only mill is off-plan. **Glarb:** A core draw-to-mill engine.

Sphinx's Tutelage.text: "Whenever you draw a card, target opponent mills two cards. If two nonland cards that share a color were milled this way, repeat this process." — **Thranduil:** Opponent mill is off-plan for a graveyard-recursion deck. **Glarb:** A core draw-to-mill engine (on `#: protect:`).

Bruvac the Grandiloquent.text: "If an opponent would mill one or more cards, they mill twice that many cards instead." — **Thranduil:** Doubles opponent mill only; T mills itself. **Glarb:** In list: the mill doubler that halves the clock; core.

Fraying Sanity.text: "At the beginning of each end step, enchanted player mills X cards, where X is the number of cards put into their graveyard from anywhere this turn." — **Thranduil:** Opponent-mill curse; nothing in T fills their yard. **Glarb:** Repeats every turn's mill total and stacks with Bruvac/Water Crystal; a core finisher.

Ruin Crab.text: "Landfall — Whenever a land you control enters, each opponent mills three cards." — **Thranduil:** Opponent mill is off-plan. **Glarb:** A 1-drop that mills about 3 per land drop (6 with Bruvac), with no draw needed.

Traumatize.text: "Target player mills half their library, rounded down." — **Thranduil:** Can self-target for ~45 cards of fuel (Muldrotha, Izoni, Morcant's Eyes), but it's a 5-mana UU sorcery that does nothing on its own. **Glarb:** A big mill that Bruvac doubles into the whole library, and Glarb can cast it from the top.

Maddening Cacophony.text: "Each opponent mills eight cards. If this spell was kicked, instead each opponent mills half their library…" — **Thranduil:** Opponent mill is off-plan. **Glarb:** In list: a kicked finisher, and with Bruvac it mills the whole library.

Startled Awake // Persistent Nightmare.text: "Target opponent mills thirteen cards. / {3}{U}{U}: Put this card from your graveyard onto the battlefield transformed." — **Thranduil:** Opponent-only mill; off-plan. **Glarb:** Big mill (26 with Bruvac) that Glarb casts off the top, with a recursion body.

Archive Trap.text: "Target opponent mills thirteen cards." — **Thranduil:** Opponent mill is off-plan. **Glarb:** A 13-card mill that Glarb can cast from the top, and it is free after their Assassin's Trophy fetch.

Glimpse the Unthinkable.text: "Target player mills ten cards." — **Thranduil:** A cheap self-mill of ten for fuel, but card disadvantage with no body or recursion. **Glarb:** Two-mana mill of ten that Bruvac and the Water Crystal scale.

Sphinx Mindbreaker.text: "When this creature enters, each opponent mills ten cards." — **Thranduil:** Opponent mill is off-plan. **Glarb:** In list: mill 10 (20 with Bruvac); 7 mana but castable off the top.

Tasha's Hideous Laughter.text: "Each opponent exiles cards from the top of their library until … total mana value 20 or greater." — **Thranduil:** Library exile has no role in T. **Glarb:** Cheap library-exile finisher (protected); core keep.

Ulamog, the Ceaseless Hunger.text: "When you cast this spell, exile two target permanents. … defending player exiles the top twenty cards" — **Thranduil:** Elf mana can cast it but it is off-plan, and Kinnan's put skips the cast trigger. **Glarb:** A 10-mana finisher; the library exile wins, but it needs ramp or Glarb's top.

The Master of Lake-town.text: "Whenever a player loses life, that player mills that many cards." — **Thranduil:** Self-mill from shocks and Yawgmoth life payments is incidental; the opponent-side mill is off-plan. **Glarb:** Turns damage, drains and Sheoldred's draw tax into mill; a deathtouch blocker.

Ashiok, Nightmare Weaver.text: "+2: Exile the top three cards of target opponent's library. −X: Put a creature card … exiled with Ashiok onto the battlefield…" — **Thranduil:** Castable, but library exile and theft do nothing for the graveyard engine. **Glarb:** In list: 3 mana for repeated library exile plus a stolen creature.

Consuming Aberration.text: "power and toughness are each equal to the number of cards in your opponents' graveyards. / Whenever you cast a spell, each opponent reveals … puts those cards into …" — **Thranduil:** T never fills the opponent's yard, so it is a mid-sized body; below the bar. **Glarb:** Every spell mills them and it grows with the milled yard; strong keep.

Rhystic Study.text: "Whenever an opponent casts a spell, you may draw a card unless that player pays {1}." — **Thranduil:** Card advantage, but in 1v1 the tax is often paid, and draws are not its engine. **Glarb:** Every draw it forces also mills through the Tutelages and Corrosion.

Mystic Remora.text: "Whenever an opponent casts a noncreature spell, you may draw a card unless that player pays {4}." — **Thranduil:** Blue card flow with upkeep tax in a creature-mana list; no synergy. **Glarb:** Cheap early draw engine, and each draw mills via the Tutelages/Corrosion.

Phyrexian Arena.text: "At the beginning of your upkeep, you draw a card and lose 1 life." — **Thranduil:** Steady card advantage (the first axis under the synergy-first rule), but plain, with no graveyard tie-in. **Glarb:** In list: an extra draw every turn means an extra mill trigger every turn.

Dictate of Kruphix.text: "At the beginning of each player's draw step, that player draws an additional card." — **Thranduil:** Symmetric draw hands the opponent cards with no payoff for T. **Glarb:** Each of our draws mills via Corrosion and their extra draw shortens their library; deliberate keep.

Teferi's Ageless Insight.text: "If you would draw a card except the first one … draw two cards instead." — **Thranduil:** Doubles Thranduil's loot (4 drawn, 1 discarded), but it is a 4-mana do-nothing alone. **Glarb:** Doubles every extra draw, so it doubles every mill trigger.

Notion Thief.text: "If an opponent would draw a card except the first one they draw in each of their draw steps, instead that player skips that draw and you draw a card." — **Thranduil:** A 4-mana U/B flash body with no graveyard or Elf synergy. **Glarb:** Turns Dictate of Kruphix's symmetric draw one-sided: every extra draw is ours and mills them.

Brainstorm.text: "Draw three cards, then put two cards from your hand on top of your library…" — **Thranduil:** Weak without shuffles; it puts cards back instead of binning them. **Glarb:** In list: three draws are three Corrosion or Tutelage triggers, and it feeds Reed Richards.

Kaito, Bane of Nightmares.text: "0: Surveil 2. Then draw a card for each opponent who lost life this turn. / −2: Tap target creature. Put two stun counters on it." — **Thranduil:** Surveil 2 a turn bins Elves and the stun is interaction; competes for a slot. **Glarb:** Surveil feeds Matoya/Proft draws, plus stun interaction and a hexproof body; strong keep.

Drown in the Loch.text: "mana value less than or equal to the number of cards in its controller's graveyard" — **Thranduil:** Scales off the opponent's yard, which this deck does not fill. **Glarb:** The opponent's milled yard makes it an unconditional counter or kill for 2.

Counterspell.text: "Counter target spell." — **Thranduil:** UU is hard on ~2 Islands plus the U duals; this mana is better spent on B/G removal. **Glarb:** Hard counter in a control list.

Thought Collapse.text: "Counter target spell. Its controller mills three cards." — **Thranduil:** A {U}{U} counter in a G/B-weighted list; interaction, but off-colour-weight. **Glarb:** In list: a counter plus mill 3 (6 with Bruvac).

Hero's Downfall.text: "Destroy target creature or planeswalker." — **Thranduil:** Instant creature/planeswalker removal; a strong add to T's interaction. **Glarb:** Flexible instant removal; strong keep.

Assassin's Trophy.text: "Destroy target permanent an opponent controls." — **Thranduil:** A 2-mana answer to any permanent. **Glarb:** A 2-mana answer to anything, and the fetch it gives turns on Archive Trap.

Cyclonic Rift.text: "Return target nonland permanent you don't control to its owner's hand. Overload {6}{U}" — **Thranduil:** The Elf mana engines make the 7-mana one-sided overload realistic; the cheap mode is only tempo. **Glarb:** Flexible one-sided bounce, and the overload is a reset.

Damnation.text: "Destroy all creatures." — **Thranduil:** Kills the deck's own Elf mana base and Thranduil; the reanimation to rebuild exists, but it fights the go-wide board. **Glarb:** In list: a board wipe for a control deck with few creatures that matter.

Breach the Multiverse.text: "Each player mills ten cards. For each player, choose a creature or planeswalker card in that player's graveyard. Put those cards onto the battlefield under your control." — **Thranduil:** Self-mill 10 plus two reanimations (pick a non-Elf from our yard); a big graveyard payoff the mana Elves reach. **Glarb:** Mills them 10 (doubled) and steals their best; but mills our own library 10 in a mill race; real.

Theorix Charm.text: "Counter … unless its controller pays {2} / -2/-2 / Mill three cards, then draw a card" — **Thranduil:** A flexible instant whose mill-3-draw mode stocks the yard. **Glarb:** Flexible interaction; the draw mode triggers mill but self-mills 3.

Arcane Signet.text: "{T}: Add one mana of any color in your commander's color identity." — **Thranduil:** Plain rock in a list with ~12 creature mana sources that do more. **Glarb:** Fixing ramp toward Glarb's MV 4+ top-deck casts.

Talisman of Dominance.text: "{T}: Add {U} or {B}. This artifact deals 1 damage to you." — **Thranduil:** T's ramp comes from Elves; a rock is below the bar. **Glarb:** In list: a 2-mana rock towards the MV 4+ top-deck casts.

Talisman of Curiosity.text: "{T}: Add {G} or {U}. This artifact deals 1 damage to you." — **Thranduil:** T ramps with mana Elves that Thranduil borrows; a rock is below the bar. **Glarb:** Two-mana ramp/fixing toward MV4+ casts; a real slot-competitor.

Mind Stone.text: "{T}: Add {C}. {1}, {T}, Sacrifice this artifact: Draw a card." — **Thranduil:** The deck's Elf mana makes a colourless rock redundant. **Glarb:** Ramp toward Glarb's 4+ casts that later cycles into a draw.

Birds of Paradise.text: "{T}: Add one mana of any color." — **Thranduil:** A 1-drop that fixes all three colours (Kinnan adds); not an Elf, but mana is synergy. **Glarb:** A 1-drop fixer, though green is the splash.

Growth Spiral.text: "Draw a card. You may put a land card from your hand onto the battlefield." — **Thranduil:** Instant ramp plus a cantrip that turns on Sindarin Liege's landfall; a real playable. **Glarb:** In list: a draw trigger plus ramp at instant speed.

Jidoor, Aristocratic Capital // Overture.text: "Target opponent mills half their library, rounded down. / This land enters tapped. {T}: Add {U}." — **Thranduil:** Tapped mono-U land whose spell is opponent mill; below the bar. **Glarb:** A land slot that mills half a library (all of it with Bruvac); strong keep.

Restless Reef.text: "Whenever this land attacks, target player mills four cards." — **Thranduil:** A tapped U/B land whose attack mill is mostly off-plan. **Glarb:** A tapped U/B land that becomes a mill-4 deathtouch attacker (8 with Bruvac).

Sunken Hollow.text: "This land enters tapped unless you control two or more basic lands." — **Thranduil:** U/B is the lightest pair, and it is usually untapped (15 basics) but adds nothing. **Glarb:** Usually untapped with 14 basics; the pair is fine.
